#### Modeling and prediction equations {#sec-pri-616}

[**Parameter Estimates Don't Change as Additional Terms Added**]{#sec-pri-616-yates}

In most cases of least-squares fitting, the model coefficient estimates for previously added terms change depending on what was successively added. For example, the estimate for the $X_1$ coefficient might change depending on whether or not an $X_2$ term was included in the model. This is **not** the case when the design is orthogonal, as is this $2^3$ full factorial design. In such a case, the estimates for the previously included terms do not change as additional terms are added. This means the list of effect estimates in [the Estimate main and interaction effects section](#sec-pri-615-yatestable) serves as the least-squares coefficient estimates for progressively more complicated models.

[**Default Model: Grand Mean**]{#sec-pri-616-default}

If none of the factors are important, the prediction equation defaults to the mean of all the response values (the overall or grand mean). That is,

$$\hat{Y} = 2.65875$$

For our example, the default model has a grand mean of 2.65875 with a residual standard deviation (a measure of goodness of fit) of 1.74106 ohms.

[**Possible Prediction Equations**]{#sec-pri-616-predeq}

We add effects to the default model in decreasing order of absolute magnitude and compute the residual standard deviation after adding each effect. The prediction equations and their residual standard deviations are shown below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pri-616-rsd-sequence
#| tbl-cap: "Cumulative residual standard deviation for progressively more complicated models"
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

eddy <- read_table(
  here::here("datasets", "SPLETT3.DAT"),
  skip = 25,
  col_names = c("y", "x1", "x2", "x3", "run_sequence"),
  col_types = "diiii"
) |>
  mutate(x1x2 = x1 * x2, x1x3 = x1 * x3, x2x3 = x2 * x3, x1x2x3 = x1 * x2 * x3)

model_terms <- c(
  "Mean + X1", "Mean + X1 + X2", "Mean + X1 + X2 + X2*X3",
  "Mean + X1 + X2 + X2*X3 + X1*X3", "Mean + X1 + X2 + X2*X3 + X1*X3 + X3",
  "Mean + X1 + X2 + X2*X3 + X1*X3 + X3 + X1*X2*X3",
  "Mean + X1 + X2 + X2*X3 + X1*X3 + X3 + X1*X2*X3 + X1*X2"
)
formulas <- list(
  y ~ x1, y ~ x1 + x2, y ~ x1 + x2 + x2x3,
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x2x3 + x1x3, y ~ x1 + x2 + x2x3 + x1x3 + x3,
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x2x3 + x1x3 + x3 + x1x2x3,
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x2x3 + x1x3 + x3 + x1x2x3 + x1x2
)
rsd_vals <- map_chr(formulas, function(f) {
  s <- summary(lm(f, data = eddy))$sigma
  if (is.na(s)) "NA" else as.character(round(s, 5))
})

tibble(`Model Terms` = model_terms, `Residual Std. Dev.` = rsd_vals) |>
  gt()
```

Note that the full model is a perfect fit to the data.
